notes:
The big one for iPad: Family D now carries the **full desktop keyboard** — ⌘K, the complete chord table, a real menu bar and the cheat sheet — plus focused-block **zoom**, desktop-style search/settings overlays, and the **Shell Parity Program** that pins iPad↔desktop behavior as a CI gate. On desktop, **in-note Find (⌘F)** arrives. Mobile gets a motion pass, a settings sweep, and swipe-to-re-parent.

**New**

- **Find in your note — ⌘F.** A dedicated in-note find bar: type to highlight every match live, ↵/⇧↵ to step through with wrap-around and a current-match ring, Esc to close. Scoped to what you're looking at (the note, a zoomed subtree, or one journal day), it reaches collapsed sections and matches inside wikilink/tag/reference chips — desktop first, behind the `find_in_note` flag. (PRD Addendum 38, F1; #949.)
- **The desktop keyboard on iPad.** Family D gains the full ⌘K command registry, the complete desktop chord table, a real menu bar, and the keyboard cheat sheet — plus the SPR-M-KB keyboard core on iPhone. (Shell Parity §W4; #804, #908, #909, #904.)
- **Zoom on iPadOS.** Focused-block zoom comes to iPad — the gutter marker, the focused view, and a tab that remembers what it zoomed into. (PRD Addendum 20; #880, #900.)
- **Swipe a row to re-parent it** (mobile, behind `block_touch`) — drag left/right to indent or outdent a block. (PRD Addendum 19 §S6, SPR-27; #878.)
- **A meta line under the note title** shows the note's mention count and folder, and the Cmd+K mention chip jumps you straight to the references. (DEC-833, SPR-37; #968.)

**Fixes & polish**

- **iPad search and settings open like the desktop** — as in-place overlays, not full-screen mobile surfaces. (SPR-28; #802, #807, #808, #865.)
- **Calmer motion on mobile** — reduced-motion honored, instant retrace, and the D-12 "only a tab you can see zooms" grammar. (#887, #888, #889, #907, #890.)
- **Settings sweep** — a back affordance, honest confirmation dialogs, AutoFill, and a batch of P3 papercuts. (#915, #922.)
- **The EditBar behaves with a hardware keyboard** — it hides on attach and restores on detach, with no launch flash or stranded bar. (#809, #935.)
- **All Notes and Browse remember your scroll** across a tab switch. (#863, #936; and BrowsePage no longer restores from a stale previous row, #940, #948.)
- **Safe mode is sturdier** — the feedback/report route survives a failed vault open, and safe mode is entered on a genuine core failure rather than a fragile heuristic. (#867, #868, #869, #922, #965.)
- **Destructive-last menus** — the note ⋯ menu lists Archive/Unarchive above Delete. (#945, #956.)
- **Esc keeps your place** — closing the palette no longer scrolls the editor to top or collapses the caret to the start; one Esc closes exactly one layer. (#814, #816, #818, #819, #820, #877, #943, #957.)
- **Delete-forever asks first**, with a real confirmation. (#884, #921.)
- Rollout-flagged menu items no longer appear inert on channels where they're off. (#950, #960.)

**Under the hood**

- **Shell Parity Program** — a 361-row desktop↔mobile behavior contract, an advisory CI ledger that flags parity drift, and the P6b test suites that pin the rows (both engines). (#926–#929, #942–#947, #964, #967, #968.)
- **Leaner CI** — path-based job filtering so a PR runs only what it touches, plus a self-hosted arm64 runner for the frontend job to cut hosted-runner load. (#969, #975.)
- **Decisions-execution rulings** SPR-35…39 + D-13 (mobile settings, journal window, mention layer, safe-mode gate, Dynamic Type, open-in-new-tab). (#958, #964.)
- Local iOS test-runner scripts (the interim gate before the macOS CI lane), a cost-gated macOS lane, Postmortem-0011, and ADR-0023 (the Escape layer stack). (#962, #879, #918, #652, #885.)
